description: World map (Equal Earth projection) of the share of households owning a dog in 43 selected countries, 2024 to 2026, in four colour groups. Countries without selected data are grey. Australia is labelled.

title.description: The big heading and the smaller line under it. On a phone they split into shorter lines.

subtitle.signal: ['Share of households owning a dog in 43 selected countries, 2024 to 2026.', 'Survey methods differ. Grey, including Malaysia: no data in this selection.']

usermeta.readMe: Vega ignores this box. It holds plain-language notes for the parts of the chart that cannot carry their own "description".

scales.steps: Turns a colour group number (0 to 3) into a colour, from pale (low) to dark (high), in the site's red-brown sequential colours. "lab" mixing makes the steps look evenly spaced to the eye.

usermeta.codeGuide: Signals set the responsive layout and theme. Data transforms derive values; scales map them to positions and colours; marks draw the chart.

projections.worldProjection: Equal Earth projection, fitted so every country shape fills the map box.

usermeta.clickSelection: story-interactions.js pins a main-mark selection in pinnedKey and clears it on an empty-space click. Species hues, quantitative colours, symbol areas and plotted positions retain their meanings.

signals.name: colorChartPanel
signals.description: Colour: the light grey chart background, used where outlines, halos or label boxes should blend into it. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-chart-panel in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetDogsLight
signals.description: Colour: the palest shade of the site's sequential colours, for low values. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-light in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorPetDogsDark
signals.description: Colour: the darkest shade of the site's sequential colours, for high values. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-dark in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorAccent
signals.description: Colour: the blue highlight colour, used for the one thing we want you to notice. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-accent in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorMuted
signals.description: Colour: the dark grey colour of small text: labels, axis words and notes. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-muted in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorHeading
signals.description: Colour: the dark blue colour of chart titles. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorBorder
signals.description: Colour: light grey, used for gridlines, empty squares and places with no data. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-border in css/style.css.

signals.name: colorSurface
signals.description: Colour: white, the colour of the card each chart sits on. This is only a backup; the real colour comes from --color-surface in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontHeading
signals.description: Font: the fancy title font (DM Serif Display). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-heading in css/style.css.

signals.name: fontBody
signals.description: Font: the plain font for all other text (Fira Sans). This is only a backup; the real font comes from --font-body in css/style.css.

signals.name: width
signals.description: How wide the chart is. It starts as the width of the box on the page and updates whenever the browser window is resized.

signals.name: narrow
signals.description: True when the chart is less than 760 pixels wide (for example on a phone). Other parts check it to use shorter words and a tighter layout.

signals.name: worldWidth
signals.description: How wide the world map is: the full width of the chart.

signals.name: worldHeight
signals.description: How tall the world map is: 40% of its width, which suits the world without Antarctica (the map file leaves Antarctica out).

signals.name: legendY
signals.description: How far down the colour key starts: just under the map.

signals.name: legendWidth
signals.description: How wide the colour key is: the full width on a phone, at most 640 pixels on a computer.

signals.name: legendColumns
signals.description: How many colour boxes sit side by side in the key: 2 on a phone, 5 (one row) on a computer.

signals.name: height
signals.description: How tall the whole chart is: the map, then the key title, then the rows of key boxes.

signals.name: hoverIso
signals.description: Remembers which country the mouse is pointing at (by its three-letter code), so that country gets a dark outline. It is cleared when the mouse leaves.

signals.name: selectedCountry
signals.description: Country chosen with the keyboard-accessible page dropdown.

signals.name: focusIso
signals.description: Pinned selection takes precedence over hover and the page-control selection.

signals.name: pinnedKey
signals.description: Main-mark selection pinned by a click. Empty chart space clears it; the loader preserves it across responsive redraws.

signals.name: legendTextSize
signals.description: Shared legend text size from --legend-text-size in css/style.css.

signals.name: legendTextWeight
signals.description: Shared legend text weight from --legend-text-weight in css/style.css.

signals.name: legendRowHeight
signals.description: Keep legend rows clear when text is enlarged to remain readable on small phones.

data.name: ownership
data.description: The survey numbers: one row per country per pet, with the share of households owning that pet.

transform.description: Turn the two rows per country (dogs, cats) into one row with a "Dogs" and a "Cats" column.
Use one consistent measured attribute across countries: the share of households owning a dog.
Kosovo has the code XKX in the survey file but KOS in the map file. This makes them match.
Two country names are shortened in the survey file. This writes them out in full words.
transform.expr: {'Rep. of Moldova': 'Republic of Moldova', 'Bosnia & Herzegovina': 'Bosnia and Herzegovina'}[datum.country] || datum.country

transform.description: Rank the countries from highest to lowest (1 = highest). Countries with the same value share a rank.

data.name: countries
data.description: The country shapes for the world map. Each shape gets its survey number glued on, if the country has one.

transform.description: Copy each shape's three-letter country code into a field called "iso", so it can be matched with the survey numbers.
Find each shape's survey numbers by its country code. Countries with no survey get empty values (not zero).
Put each country into a colour group: 0 = under 25%, 1 = 25% to 34%, 2 = 35% to 44%, 3 = 45% or more, and -1 = no survey.

data.name: australia
data.description: Just Australia, picked out of the country shapes so it can get its own label.

data.name: legend
data.description: The five entries in the colour key: four colour groups and "No selected data".

projections.name: worldProjection
projections.description: How the round Earth is flattened onto the flat screen. "Equal Earth" keeps every country's area fair, so big countries do not look bigger than they are. It is stretched to fill the map space.

marks.name: worldPanel
marks.description: The box that holds the world map. Anything outside it is cut off.

marks.name: worldPanelShapes
marks.description: The country shapes, coloured by their colour group. Countries with no selected data are see-through grey. Hover shows the values.
